subject: Renewal: frequency-banded discounting & renewal roadmap
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@borealhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning + frequency-banded discounts

Laura —

We’re coming up on the end of year renewal for Boreal Health (deal BRHL-2026-1024) and our finance team asked whether Redwood supports a frequency-banded discounting approach instead of a flat per-token tier. Specifically:

- Can discounts vary by usage cadence (baseline vs burst periods)?
- Can we smooth uplift at renewal (we’ve seen big seasonal spikes) so that % increases year-over-year are capped?
- What true-up cadence do you support (monthly vs quarterly) and how does that affect pricing?

We’re open to a committed spend but want a right-size option that recognizes our quarterly campaign spikes. Can you share a proposal or banding example?

Thanks —
Olivia Chen
Head of Procurement
Boreal Health

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@borealhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + frequency-banded discounts

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clear ask. We do support frequency-banded discounting and a few pragmatic renewal guardrails that map to what you describe. I’m attaching a short example offer (Redwood_Frequency_Bands_Offer_V2.pdf) and the usage profile you requested.

High-level options we typically propose:

1) Band-based commit (recommended for seasonality):
   - Baseline band (committed) covers 70% of historical avg monthly usage at X% discount.
   - Seasonal band (buffer) covers up to +30% above baseline at a smaller discount.
   - Burst band (on-demand) billed at list with a small burst charge to discourage chronic overage.

2) Uplift cap and smoothing:
   - We can cap renewal uplift to a negotiated % (common starting point 10–15%).
   - Option: 12-month smoothing window that averages your trailing 12 months before applying uplift.

3) True-up cadence: monthly (preferred for high variability) or quarterly (standard). Monthly true-ups add operational overhead but reduce surprise at year-end.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll loop in Aditya (SE) and Finance (Vivek) for sizing and a final offer;
- If you confirm preferred true-up cadence and an uplift cap range (e.g., 8–12%), we’ll produce Offer_V2 for signatures.

Attachments: Redwood_Frequency_Bands_Offer_V2.pdf (pricing table + example bands), Redwood_Usage_Profile_Q3.csv (you provided earlier, annotated).

Best,
Laura Bennett

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@borealhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + frequency-banded discounts

Hi team —

I took a look at the usage profile (attached) and ran a quick simulation of three commit shapes: baseline-only, baseline+seasonal buffer, and committed baseline + burst buffer. Key findings:

- Boreal’s 95th percentile month over the past 12 months is ~3.4x their median month; spikes are short (2–3 days).
- Baseline covering 65–75% of median month with a 10–20% seasonal buffer gives the best cost predictability while keeping on-demand exposure low.
- We recommend a 10% continuous burst buffer (auto-burst cap) to protect latency SLO during campaign peaks; billing for the burst buffer is at a modest premium but avoids throttling.

Operational notes: monthly true-up increases bookkeeping but lets procurement align cashflow; quarterly true-up is less operationally noisy but can create larger year-end true-ups.

I’ve attached the usage CSV with spike annotations: Redwood_Usage_Profile_Q3.csv (see column "spike_reason").

If the customer wants a hard renewal uplift ceiling, a 10% cap is defensible; if they want a firmer guarantee we can move to 8% but would need a slightly larger baseline commit to compensate (or a longer smoothing window).

Happy to join a 30-min call to walk through the numbers.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal planning + frequency-banded discounts

Tom —

Thanks — good negotiation points. Quick summary of what we can offer as a compromise so legal has something concrete: 

- Renewal uplift cap: 10% annual cap by default; we can offer 8% cap if Boreal agrees to a 6-month smoothing window (12-month trailing average applied at renewal) or a 7% incremental baseline uplift at signature to reduce risk for Redwood.
- True-up cadence: monthly true-ups — accepted. We’ll provide monthly statements and an automated token-level export.
- Payment terms: Net-45 standard for negotiated deals; we can accept Net-30 in exchange for a 1% payment term concession to preserve economics.
- SLA / audit logs: we will provide token-level cost reporting (downloadable CSV) and audit log access via the Console for the contract term; details to be captured in the SOW.

I’ve attached Offer_V2 (Redwood_Frequency_Bands_Offer_V2.pdf) with inline redlines for the uplift smoothing option and payment terms. If you confirm which uplift path you prefer (hard 8% + 6-month smoothing OR 10% straight cap), Marissa and I will finalize and send via DocuSign.

Next steps:
- Tom / Olivia confirm uplift path and acceptance of Net-30 with 1% fee OR Net-45 no fee;
- We’ll circulate the final PDF and DocuSign link.

Looking forward —
